title: Q&A cards
headline: We answer the 13 likely questions plainly, with a suggested speaker for each: the base case misses F1 and the extra revenue is our assumption.

items.head: Q1 Why back a plan that misses F1 and does not repay?
items.text: A gated test. The no-plan path also misses F1 (6.0% growth, 35.2% margin). Only ฿240m of tactics repay; benefits after FY2028E are not valued.

items.head: Q2 Does the plan pay for itself?
items.text: No. On assumed uplift, ฿560m a year is not repaid by FY2028E (needs 67% pass-through). ฿240m of tactics repay in 1.2 years; ฿320m earns none.

items.head: Q3 Isn't our 35.5% floor inflated by one-offs? Is F1 missed on core?
items.text: Yes: FY2025 held ฿2,119m of Rama 2 one-offs (3.2 points). On the K8 core test, base 33.9% clears a 32.3% floor, but growth of 6.6% still misses 7.0%.

items.head: Q4 What evidence supports the extra revenue?
items.text: Not yet measured. Team assumptions (25% visit share for ages 18–29, +10% frequency, +5% lift) carry 79% of FY2028E uplift. Gates G2 and G3 test the lift and the active-member frequency (at least +5% each) and G4 the uplift they produce; the 25% share is not measured directly, as K1 is the 20–29 share of visitors aged 20+.

items.head: Q5 How do you know ฿2,200m is already in costs?
items.text: We do not. CPN reports no separate marketing expense, so ฿2,200m is our assumption. Each ฿100m not in the base cuts FY2027E margin by 0.14 points.

items.head: Q6 How much of the money really depends on results?
items.text: 45% of net-new (฿250m of ฿560m) waits for a results test, at G2 or G3. G0 and G1 test readiness; ฿310m (55%) is due by 30 Jun.

items.head: Q7 What stops a loss-making FY2028 repeat?
items.text: Gate G4, but only in part. It requires the tactics break-even (฿400m uplift, pass-through above 29%). The full ฿560m needs ฿933m uplift and 67% pass-through; G4 reports that test but does not require it, so a pass can release a repeat the base case does not repay (FY2028E uplift ฿696m). A miss limits FY2028 to the tactics that passed.

items.head: Q8 What is the ESG index called, and is FTSE4Good confirmed?
items.text: The Dow Jones Best-in-Class Indices (formerly DJSI): World 8 years, Emerging Markets 12, per CPN, 9 Apr 2026. FTSE4Good: per CPN, unconfirmed.

items.head: Q9 Which emissions target do you quote?
items.text: One only: a 50% cut in emissions intensity by 2034 against a 2024 base, the target in CPN's latest (2025) climate summary.

items.head: Q10 How many members does The 1 have?
items.text: Central Retail's loyalty ecosystem: 23 million members in Thailand (press release, 14 Aug 2026). It does not name the programme; we read it as The 1.

items.head: Q11 Where does the 1Q27 date for The Central Phaholyothin come from?
items.text: CPN's 2Q26 MD&A (p. 7) lists "The Central" at 1Q27, which we read as The Central Phaholyothin. Spend waits for a CPN filing (D1); other dates on B2.

items.head: Q12 Which net margin is right: 35.5% or 33.1%?
items.text: 35.5% is our calculation (18,841 / 53,009). CPN publishes 33.1% (IR page), about 35.6% (MD&A) and 36% (One Report). We never call 35.5% CPN's figure.

items.head: Q13 How is Gen Z defined, and what consent age?
items.text: Ages 18–29 (team definition). The survey reaches only people aged 20+ (age of majority; younger people would need a guardian on our reading of PDPA s.20), so it measures 20–29; member data cover active members 18–29 (18–19 provisional). DataReportal's 13–24 is a different band.

notes: Owners are suggested and can be swapped. Q1 (Spkr 6): It is a gated test, and the no-plan path also misses F1. Q2 (Spkr 4): No. On assumed uplift, the full 560 million a year is not repaid by FY2028E. Q3 (Spkr 5): Yes, our floor holds FY2025 one-offs; on the core test the margin passes, but growth still misses 7.0 percent. Q4 (Spkr 4): Not yet measured; our volume assumptions carry most of the uplift, and gates two and three test the lift and the active-member frequency, gate four the uplift they produce; the 25% share is not measured directly, because K1 is the 20 to 29 share of visitors aged 20 and over. Q5 (Spkr 1): We do not know; CPN reports no separate marketing expense, so the 2,200 million is our assumption. Q6 (Spkr 5): 45 percent of the net-new money waits for a results test, at gate two or three; gates zero and one test readiness. Q7 (Spkr 5): Gate G4, but only in part. It requires the tactics break-even, 400 million of uplift and pass-through above 29 percent. If it is missed, FY2028 is limited to the tactics that passed. The full 560 million needs 933 million of uplift and 67 percent pass-through. G4 reports that test but does not require it, so a pass can release a repeat that the base case does not repay; its FY2028E uplift is 696 million. Q8 (Spkr 2): It is the Dow Jones Best-in-Class Indices, formerly DJSI, per CPN (9 Apr 2026); S&P's Sustainability Yearbook 2026 (S&P-sourced) lists CPN in the top 10% of CSA scores. Q9 (Spkr 6): We quote only the 50% cut in emissions intensity by 2034 against 2024. Q10 (Spkr 2): Central Retail's loyalty ecosystem has 23 million members in Thailand (Central Retail press release, 14 Aug 2026), which we read as The 1. Q11 (Spkr 3): The 1Q27 date comes from the 2Q26 MD&A, p. 7; launch spend follows a CPN filing (D1). Q12 (Spkr 5): 35.5% is our own calculation from CPN's two reported figures. Q13 (Spkr 4): Gen Z and young adults are ages 18 to 29; our survey reaches only respondents aged 20 and over, the age of majority, so it measures 20 to 29, and member data cover active members 18 to 29; younger respondents would need a guardian under the PDPA, which a Thai-law reader should confirm; The 1 data for ages 18 and 19 are aggregated and provisional until then.
sources: Central Pattana, 2026a, 2026g (p. 7), 2026p, 2026t, n.d.-g (pp. 1, 5); Central Pattana Investor Relations, n.d.-c, 2026

facts.on_slide: Q1: A gated test

facts.on_slide: Q1: The no-plan path also misses F1 (6.0% growth, 35.2% margin)
facts.meaning: Without the plan, FY2027E total revenue growth would be 6.0% (7.0% is needed) and net margin 35.2% (35.24% before rounding; our floor is 35.5%), so the organic path already misses both F1 tests
facts.where: ch5.md 5.2 paragraph after Table 5.7 ('Without the plan growth would be 6.0% and 6.3%'); Table 5.10 row Net margin without the plan; 5.3 paragraph after Table 5.10

facts.on_slide: Q1 and Q2: Only ฿240m of tactics repay (1.2 years)
facts.meaning: Of the ฿560 million a year of net-new spend, ฿240 million is for the tactics that carry M1 to M4 uplift (lines 4, 6, 7 and 9 less the ฿100 million line 1 cut) and repays in 1.2 years on the base-case uplift, with the ฿240 million spent again in FY2028E (Table 5.4 cost base is a year); the other ฿320 million (opening launches, sustainability storytelling, research) earns no revenue credit
facts.where: ch5.md 5.1 paragraph 2 (opens 'The incremental cost is not the ฿2,760 million ceiling'); Table 5.4 row 1; Table 5.5 row Base

facts.on_slide: Q1: benefits after FY2028E are not valued
facts.meaning: The model values the uplift only to FY2028E; benefits beyond FY2028E are not valued
facts.where: ch5.md 5.2 paragraph after Table 5.6 (last sentence)

facts.on_slide: Q2: No. On assumed uplift, ฿560m a year is not repaid by FY2028E: it needs 67% pass-through, not the 50% assumed
facts.meaning: Net-new spend of ฿560 million a year (FY2027E and again FY2028E) is covered 75% in FY2028E and falls ฿505 million short cumulatively to FY2028E; break-even pass-through to CPN's revenue is 67% at the FY2028E run-rate against the 50% assumed; all on the base-case uplift, which is a team assumption
facts.where: ch5.md 5.1 paragraph after Table 5.4; Table 5.4 row 2; Table 5.2 rows C5 and D5

facts.on_slide: Q3: FY2025 held ฿2,119m of Rama 2 one-offs (3.2 points)
facts.meaning: FY2025 profit held Rama 2 one-offs of ฿1,234 million (other income) and ฿1,415 million (lease interest) before tax, ฿2,119 million after tax; they are 3.2 points of FY2025's 35.5% margin, which is the margin our floor is built on (team calculation, not a CPN figure)
facts.where: ch5.md chapter introduction; Table 5.2 rows A4 and V2; 5.3 paragraph after Table 5.10 ('FY2025's one-offs (3.2 points)'); ch6.md Table 6.6 row 9; model_out.txt oneoff_pts = 3.2

facts.on_slide: Q3: On the K8 core test, base 33.9% clears a 32.3% floor
facts.meaning: KPI K8 reads the margin floor on a core basis as well (core excludes Rama 2 lease interest): core floor 32.3% [Proposed], FY2025's core margin; base-path FY2027E core margin 33.9%, 1.6 points above it. The reported base margin is 34.6% against the 35.5% floor
facts.where: ch6.md Table 6.3 row K8; ch5.md Table 5.10 row Core net margin; 5.3 paragraph after Table 5.10 ('the margin rises from 32.3% to 33.9%'); model_out.txt core_gain_b27 = +1.6
facts.cite: Central Pattana, 2026p; team proposal; team calculation

facts.on_slide: Q3: growth of 6.6% still misses 7.0%
facts.meaning: The F1 revenue test (7.0% to 9.0%) is missed in the base case whichever way margin is read: FY2027E total revenue growth is 6.6%, 0.4 points short; only the optimistic case, a target by definition, meets it
facts.where: ch5.md Table 5.8 row Base; 5.2 paragraph after Table 5.7; ch6.md Table 6.3 row K9

facts.on_slide: Q4: Team assumptions (25% visit share, +10% frequency, +5% lift)
facts.meaning: Team assumptions: 25% of visits are made by the 18-29 band, Gen Z visit frequency +10% (at 50% yield), and a +5% sales lift for The 1 BIZ partner stores (16.7% of revenue). CPN publishes no Gen Z share; Chapter 6 adopts +10% and +5% as [Proposed] targets set equal to the assumptions, which are not evidence for them
facts.where: ch5.md Table 5.2 rows C1 and C4; 5.2 paragraph after Table 5.6; ch6.md Table 6.3 rows K2 and K5

facts.on_slide: Q4: 79% of FY2028E uplift
facts.meaning: In the model M1 (Gen Z) supplies 47% of the FY2028E uplift and M1 plus M4 supply 79%, so two unsourced team assumptions (Table 5.2 rows C1 and C4) carry the case
facts.where: ch5.md 5.2 paragraph after Table 5.6; model_out.txt m1_share28 = 47%, m14_share28 = 79%

facts.on_slide: Q4: Gates G2 and G3 test lift and active-member frequency; G4 tests the uplift they produce
facts.meaning: The Section 4.5 baseline is due by 31 March 2027 (G1); G2 tests the The 1 BIZ lift (at least +5% against matched controls) and S7 revenue per baht; G3 tests Gen Z visits per active member (at least +5%); G4 tests the uplift run-rate and pass-through (K12)
facts.where: ch6.md Table 6.2 rows G1 to G4; Table 6.3 rows K1, K2, K5 and K12

facts.on_slide: Q5: ฿2,200m is our assumption; CPN reports no separate marketing expense
facts.meaning: The ฿2,200 million (flagships at their latest disclosed editions of 600, 600 and 800, plus The 1 BIZ at 200) is assumed to sit in the FY2026E cost base. CPN reports one administrative-expense line and no marketing expense in the MD&A and One Report reviewed, so the figure is an assumption and an upper bound on what is embedded; it cannot be verified
facts.where: ch5.md 5.1 paragraph 2; 5.3 paragraph 1; Table 5.9 row Less: already in the FY2026E cost base; ch4.md 4.5 budget paragraph (One Report p. 192)
facts.cite: Central Pattana, 2026p; Central Pattana Investor Relations, 2026; team assumption

facts.on_slide: Q5: Each ฿100m not in the base cuts FY2027E margin by 0.14 points
facts.meaning: Each ฿100 million of marketing that is not already in the base cost base (so is net-new) lowers the FY2027E margin by about 0.14 points
facts.where: ch5.md 5.1 paragraph 2 ('each ฿100 million not in the base lowers the FY2027E margin by about 0.14 points'); 5.3 paragraph after Table 5.11; model_out.txt per100 = 0.14%

facts.on_slide: Q6: 45% of net-new (฿250m of ฿560m) waits for a results test, at G2 or G3
facts.meaning: Net-new spend by quarter is 55, 255, 130 and 120 (Table 5.9). Table 6.2 releases Q3 spend (130) at G2 and Q4 net-new (120) at G3, both gates with results tests; together 250, which is 44.6% of 560, shown as 45%
facts.where: ch5.md Table 5.9 row Net-new spend charged to SG&A; ch6.md 6.1 release rules; Table 6.1; Table 6.2 rows G2 ('Q3 spend') and G3 ('Q4 net-new of ฿120 million')

facts.on_slide: Q6: G0 and G1 test readiness; ฿310m (55%) is due by 30 Jun
facts.meaning: G0 and G1 pass tests cover set-up and baseline (Plan Office and squad leads named, data-protection plan, agency contracted, baseline report, consent live, plus the FY2026 profit check); from G2 the tests are results (The 1 BIZ lift, S7 revenue per baht and M2 registrant share at G2; Gen Z visits per active member at G3; uplift run-rate at G4). Q1 and Q2 net-new sum to 310, 55.4% of 560 (shown as 55%), due before G2 on 30 June; the 310 is not the ฿310 million of budget lines 4, 6 and 7. For reference, cumulative net-new on the quarter-by-quarter release is 55 after G0 (10%), 310 after G1 (55%), 440 after G2 (79%) and 560 after G3; Table 6.2 states the Q1 release at G0, Q3 at G2 and Q4 at G3, and the Q2 release at G1 follows the same pattern
facts.where: ch6.md Table 6.2 column Pass test, rows G0 to G4; ch5.md Table 5.9; ch6.md 6.1 release rules (58.3% of the gross ceiling is spent by 30 June)

facts.on_slide: Q12: Ages 18–29 (team definition)
facts.meaning: Gen Z and young adults are ages 18 to 29 (a team definition, not CPN's); the survey reaches only respondents aged 20 and over, so it measures ages 20 to 29, and The 1 member data (active members) cover 18 to 29

facts.on_slide: Q13: the survey reaches only people aged 20+ (age of majority; younger people would need a guardian on our reading of PDPA s.20), so it measures 20–29; member data cover active members 18–29 (18–19 provisional)
facts.meaning: The team uses the Civil Code majority of 20 as the PDPA consent age (decided 29 Oct 2026, replacing the earlier 18); the survey reaches respondents aged 20 and over, so K1 is the 20–29 share of visitors aged 20 and over and ages 18 and 19 are seen only in The 1 member data (K2, active members); the plan band stays ages 18–29 (decided 29 Oct 2026)
facts.where: corrections.md Facts, Survey consent; ch4.md 4.5 age-band and PDPA paragraphs now say 20 (report fixed 29 Oct 2026)
facts.cite: Personal Data Protection Act, B.E. 2562, 2019; team treatment

facts.on_slide: Q7: Gate G4 only in part: tactics break-even (400m uplift, pass-through above 29%); the full 560m needs 933m uplift and 67% pass-through, reported, not required; the base case does not repay a repeat (FY2028E uplift 696m)
facts.meaning: Table 6.2 G4 pass test is the tactics break-even (uplift run-rate at least 400 million, pass-through above 29%, K12); a failed G4 limits FY2028 to the tactics that passed; K12 also lists 933 million and 67% for all net-new spend, which G4 reports beside the tactics test but does not require (Table 6.2 row G4 and K12 now say so; tightening to 933 million and 67% would fail the base case, whose FY2028E uplift is 696 million, and force a re-run of FY2028E)
facts.where: ch6.md Table 6.2 row G4; Table 6.3 row K12; ch5.md section 5.1 and Table 5.4
